newsitem.title: ERITREA: Sudan rebels say capture 1,000 government soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels say capture 1,000 government soldiers.

text.p: Sudanese rebels said on Friday they had captured 1,000 government soldiers after overrunning the major town of Yei and Morobo garrison in the south.
Yassir Arman, spokesman for the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), told Reuters at rebel headquarters in the Eritrean capital Asmara that the soldiers were lured into rebel-held territory.
"The SPLA captured around 1,000 prisoners of war," said Arman. He said government troops had fled a combined rebel force.

On Thursday, Arman said the SPLA led by veteran guerrilla leader John Garang had captured Yei, biggest town in Western Equatoria region, on Wednesday after seizing Morobo garrison. Morobo is close to Sudan's borders with Zaire and Uganda.
He said SPLA forces besieged Lainya garrison, 100 km (60 miles) south of Juba and the south's biggest city, and on Thursday ambushed an army convoy between Juba and Lainya.
"The SPLA have destroyed in Kaya, Bazi, Morobo and Yei, a division of the NIF (National Islamic Front), which is about 5,000 to 6,000 men," said the rebel spokesman. He did not give rebel casualties.
In Khartoum, a cabinet minister was on Friday quoted as denying that Yei had fallen to the rebels but said there was intensive fighting in the area.

"Yei is secure," Sudanese newspapers quoted Culture and Information Minister Al-Tayeb Ibrahim Mohamed Khair as saying in a briefing on Thursday. "As for their claims that they have captured some areas, these are not towns but inspection posts."
Khair said six officers were killed at Lainya, Loka and Yei.

Arman said the SPLA had also captured 15 T-55 tanks, three BM-21 artillery pieces and two 130mm long-range artillery in recent days. The spokesman said in an ambush on a convoy on Thursday from Juba, the SPLA destroyed six trucks of NIF troops.

"We have captured a huge amount of arms from the NIF, and we are going to use them in the coming battles. When we use them, the NIF will accuse the U.S., Israel, Uganda and Eritrea of supplying us with arms, but it is the NIF which is supplying us with arms," said Arman.
Khair said weapons the rebels used in the fighting were too sophisticated to be Uganda's, Sudanese newspapers reported.
"Uganda does not possess these sophisticated weapons. Nor does it have the ability to launch the attack," he said.
Sudan's state radio quoted army spokesman Lieutenant-General Mohamad al-Sanousi Ahmed as saying on Thursday: "The military equipment used is definitely America's, so are the rations."
The Islamic-backed military government in Khartoum frequently accuses Uganda, Ethiopia and Eritrea of backing Garang rebels. All three deny the charge.
The SPLA has been fighting Khartoum since 1983, demanding greater autonomy for the mainly Christian and animist south of Sudan from the Moslem and Arabised north.
